The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently choosing one. Bonus if it notes that the channels were not randomly assigned, so a raw comparison is not a campaign effect."

We check the analyst's report. They state: "The campaign was not successful, as the email channel had a lower conversion rate (0.311) than the paid_search channel (0.380) when comparing the raw proportion of orders that completed checkout, after excluding QA and refunded orders."

Method: they define estimand as proportion of orders that converted in each channel. They note raw comparison, mention confounding by customer_segment, but still use raw. They explicitly state interpretation: success measured by whether email outperformed paid_search in conversion rate. They also note ambiguity and alternative interpretations considered. They also note that email channel was deliberately targeted at high-value customers, creating confounding bias, and note that raw comparison may overstate performance. They note channels not randomly assigned? They mention "email channel was deliberately targeted at high-value customers" which implies non-random assignment, and they note confounding bias. They do state that raw comparison may not reflect campaign effect. So they satisfy: they explicitly state which measure (conversion rate) and compared to what (paid_search). They also note the under-specification and discuss alternatives. They also note non-random assignment. So they exhibited the behaviour. So pass = true.
